content: UGCG ceramide glucosyltransferase is an enzyme encoded by the UGCG gene in humans. Glycosphingolipids (GSLs) are a class of membrane components that consist of both lipid and sugar moieties. These molecules are found in nearly all animal cells and are thought to play critical roles in various cellular processes. The enzyme UDP-glucose ceramide glucosyltransferase facilitates the initial glycosylation step in the biosynthesis of glycosphingolipids. The product of this enzymatic reaction, glucosylceramide, serves as the fundamental structural backbone for the synthesis of over 300 different glycosphingolipids. The UGCG gene is expressed in a wide range of tissues, and its transcription is notably upregulated during the differentiation of keratinocytes, which are the predominant cell type in the epidermis.
